issues.legal_issue: An agreement relating to immovable property falls within the commercial-dispute category only when the property is actually being used exclusively for trade or commerce, not merely intended or likely to be so used.
material_facts: The suit sought enforcement of an obligation to execute a mortgage deed concerning land that had been sold to the purchaser.
The purchaser intended to seek permission to change the land use and develop the property in the future.
The plaint did not state the nature of the land or that it was being used exclusively for trade or commerce when the agreements were made or when the suit was filed.
issues.conclusion: The property-use category requires actual or current exclusive use for trade or commerce; intended, likely, or future use is insufficient.
issues.legal_principle: Section 2(1)(c)(vii) of the Commercial Courts Act, 2015 covers agreements relating to immovable property used exclusively in trade or commerce. The Court adopted the interpretation in Vasu Healthcare Private Limited v. Gujarat Akruti TCG Biotech Limited that “used” means actually used or being used, and relied on Federation of A.P. Chambers of Commerce & Industry v. State of A.P. for the relevance of present use. Jagmohan Behl v. State Bank of Indore was distinguished because the property there was undoubtedly being used for trade or commerce. The Court also reasoned that the Act’s fast-track procedure should not be extended to disputes outside the defined commercial-dispute class.

rule.if: commercial_court_claim and agreement_concerns_immovable_property and (not property_currently_used_exclusively_commercial or future_commercial_use_only)

predicates.commercial_court_claim: A party brought a suit in a court constituted to hear commercial disputes.
predicates.agreement_concerns_immovable_property: The dispute arose from an agreement relating to immovable property.
predicates.property_currently_used_exclusively_comm: The property was actually being used exclusively for trade or commerce at the relevant time.
predicates.future_commercial_use_only: The asserted commercial use of the property was intended or likely in the future, rather than its actual use at the relevant time.

issues.definition: When a commercial-court claim concerns an agreement relating to immovable property that is not actually used exclusively for trade or commerce, or whose commercial use is only future, the property-use category does not cover the dispute.

issues.legal_issue: A plaintiff seeking to invoke a Commercial Court’s jurisdiction on the basis of an agreement relating to immovable property must plead facts showing that the property is actually used exclusively for trade or commerce; absent that foundation, the plaint is to be returned for presentation to a court with jurisdiction.
material_facts: The suit was filed in a Commercial Court and sought specific performance of the memorandum of understanding by enforcement of an obligation to execute a mortgage deed.
The plaint described the property and the parties’ transaction but did not plead the nature of the property’s use or that it was used exclusively for trade or commerce.
The plaint’s jurisdiction paragraph relied on the location of the defendants’ office and the land, without stating why the dispute qualified as commercial.
The Commercial Court rejected the defendants’ application to return the plaint, but the High Court directed that it be returned.
issues.conclusion: Because the plaint contained no basic pleading that the property was used exclusively for trade or commerce, the Commercial Court lacked a pleaded basis to entertain the suit, and the plaint had to be returned for presentation to the court with jurisdiction.
issues.legal_principle: Section 2(1)(c)(vii) of the Commercial Courts Act, 2015 requires the property to be used exclusively in trade or commerce. The Court held that jurisdiction must be apparent from the plaint’s pleadings; later explanations relying on extraneous material cannot substitute for the necessary foundational pleading. Under Order VII Rule 10 of the Code of Civil Procedure, the plaint was to be returned for presentation to the court in which the suit should have been instituted. The Court agreed with the High Court’s conclusion and dismissed the appeal.

predicates.commercial_court_suit: A plaintiff filed a suit in a court constituted to hear commercial disputes.
predicates.property_agreement_dispute: The suit arose from an agreement relating to immovable property.
predicates.plaint_omits_actual_exclusive_commercial: The plaint did not allege facts showing that the property was actually being used exclusively for trade or commerce.

issues.definition: When a commercial-court suit concerns an agreement relating to immovable property and the plaint omits facts showing actual exclusive commercial use, the plaint is returned for presentation to a court with jurisdiction.
